newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HORN DEFENDS SACKING OF CENTRAL BANK OFFICIALS.
newsitem.headline: HORN DEFENDS SACKING OF CENTRAL BANK OFFICIALS.

text.p: Hungarian prime minister Gyula Horn on Tuesday defended his decision to accept the resignations of two top bank officials over a miscalculated options deal made four years ago.

National Bank of Hungary vice presidents Frigyes Harshegyi and Sandor Czirjak resigned last week after an internal NBH report disclosed a foreign exchange contract with Creditanstalt Investment Fund concluded in 1992 that is expected to cost the central bank billions of forints.
"On the basis of what we heard the two vice presidents had to take responsibility and I accepted (their resignations) because I could not do anything else," Horn told reporters.

The contract was for foreign exchange rate guarantees maturing in 1998 in which the partners shared forint devaluation risks while Creditinstalt did not have to pay an option fee, a decision which the NBH said could cost it more than three billion forints.

The NBH report was submitted to the Cabinet by NBH President Gyorgy Suranyi who recommended that Horn turn down Harshegyi and Czirjak's offers of resignation in view of the high level of their work since they were appointed in 1991.
Horn rejected Suranyi's advice and accepted the two men's resignation immediately instead of waiting until the end of their contracts.
"The two vice presidents have made a lot of good decisions and brought a lot of good things to the country but this was a case in which you could not defer responsibility," Horn said on Tuesday.
The news came hard on the heels of a scandal over payments of millions of dollars by the state privatisation agency APV Rt to a consultant, Marta Tocsik.

That revelation led to the dismissal of the entire APV board and the minister in charge and amalysts have speculated that Harshegyi and Czirjak would have been treated less harshly but for the public pressure on the governemt from the Tocsik case.
